title: K.P. Energy Ltd - 539686 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

segments.name: Infrastructure development (EPC)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs. 504.75 crore in Q1 FY27 vs Rs. 208.25 crore in Q1 FY26, ~142% growth; management calls it the growth engine. About 50% of order book by value is related party.

segments.name: O&M
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs. 2.94 crore vs Rs. 1.16 crore a year earlier. Management cites it as a recurring revenue stream to be strengthened.

segments.name: Sale of power (IPP)
segments.commentary: Revenue Rs. 11.78 crore vs Rs. 10.14 crore in Q1 FY26. IPP capacity is 48.5 MW fully operational (11.5 MW solar, 37 MW wind); IPP is ~2% of total revenue per management.

qa_highlights.question: Will margins revert to Q4/Q3 levels or is Q1 the new normal? Can margins recover to 15-18%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 is not fully representative but would not assume immediate normalisation; it declined to give a margin number, citing stage-mix dependence, and said costs already seen since end-Q4 FY26 are built into Q1 cost.

qa_highlights.question: Is the top-line growth guidance of 40-50% still valid?
qa_highlights.answer: Management revised guidance to about 30-40% as a cautious scenario; internal target is to complete a substantial part of the existing order book in FY27, and it said ROW protests could limit execution.

qa_highlights.question: Why has order inflow been slower than on-ground wind activity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is picking orders selectively based on cost components, execution capability, region and grid/ROW costs; about 230+ MW was won in Q4 FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Current IPP portfolio and expansion plans?
qa_highlights.answer: 48.5 MW operational (11.5 MW solar, 37 MW wind); about 200 MW to be added through two 100 MW PPA-backed projects, roughly 24 months from April 2026 onward.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBITDA margin fall so sharply, and are the orders cost pass-through?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said contracts are fixed-price, not cost-plus, though some have force majeure clauses; it asked investors not to treat Q1 as the benchmark and said no foresight can be given on net margin.

qa_highlights.question: Reconciliation of order book from about Rs. 3,000 crore last quarter to Rs. 2,250 crore, and value disclosure for new orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about Rs. 500 crore was executed in Q1, leaving about Rs. 2,500 crore, and a further Rs. 250 crore gap is under review for possible de-scoping; clients often bar disclosure of order values.

guidance_outlook: FY27 top-line growth guided at about 30% to 40%, cut from the earlier 40% to 50%; management calls this a cautious scenario and says internal targets are to complete a substantial part of the order book this year.

Management said Q1 is not an exact representative going forward but declined to guide on a margin number or to assume immediate normalisation; it expects to offset cost pressure through operating efficiency.

Two IPP projects of 100 MW each under PPAs with sovereign entities (one signed April 2026, one July 2026), roughly 24-month execution; partial commissioning could bring revenue about one year in. Management expects IPP revenue to rise by about Rs. 200 crore once both are energised.
Management said it expects 100 MW of IPP capacity by end-FY27 (in response to a question), and 248.5 MW (48.5 MW plus 200 MW) over about two years.
Group target of 10 GW by 2030 is described as very close to achievement; a revised group target and company-specific targets are to be published soon.
Management expects new order inflows in about 6 to 9 months and says it is picking orders selectively.
capex_capacity: Order book of 2.16 GW as of end-Q1 FY27, valued at about Rs. 2,250 crore as of June 30, 2026 (vs about Rs. 3,000 crore last quarter per management's reconciliation; about Rs. 500 crore executed in Q1).
Commissioned the 50.4 MW Vanki Wind Project in Kutch in July 2026.
Standalone IPP capacity is 48.5 MW, fully operational; plan to add about 200 MW via two 100 MW PPA-backed projects with 24-month timelines.

Karnataka identified as first expansion beyond Gujarat; management said about 30% of the related work has been acquired, with connectivity, land and EHV/PSS tied up, and a notification is expected soon.
Management said it is also developing BESS services to mitigate curtailment risk.
demand_pricing: Order book 2.16 GW, about Rs. 2,250 crore; management says it is being selective and has slowed order intake to avoid low-margin or resource-blocking orders.
About 230+ MW of orders were won in Q4 FY26, per management.

Q1 margin pressure attributed to West Asia/Strait of Hormuz disruption (LPG, fuel, freight, manpower), fuel availability for cranes and equipment, and higher transmission right-of-way (ROW) compensation after Gujarat farmer protests and a revised government framework.

Management said most contracts are fixed-price; some have force majeure provisions, and it is exploring force majeure or price relief where possible, but gave no generalised answer on escalation clauses.
Management said industry margins of several renewable EPC peers have fallen by 12%, 7% and 4% (unnamed).
risks_watch: Gross margin compression (~20% vs 28% in Q4 FY26) with no margin guidance; watch Q2 FY27 margin and PAT trend.
Transmission ROW compensation escalation following Gujarat protests and revised framework; may delay execution.
Grid and transmission bottlenecks and government curtailment; management plans BESS services as mitigation.
Monsoon seasonality in Q2 and fuel/LPG supply volatility affecting equipment utilisation.
Related-party concentration: about 50% of order book by value is from related parties.
Possible de-scoping of about Rs. 250 crore of existing order book value; order book fell from about Rs. 3,000 crore to Rs. 2,250 crore.
Leadership transition with incoming Group CFO Kapil Kriplani; watch timing of revised company-specific targets and the separate KP Green Engineering disclosures.
key_quotes: We believe it is important to explain this.
Our order book at the end of Q1 FY27 stands at 2.16 GW, providing a strong revenue visibility.
And we do not envisage any kind of an immediate further fall.
I would like to summarize, stating that the scale of the business has changed materially.
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term opportunity and execution, but cautious and non-committal on near-term margins and top-line, repeatedly declining to give margin numbers and cutting FY27 growth guidance to 30-40%. Defensive when questioned on governance, promoter visibility and related-party orders, and attributes margin pressure to industry-wide factors.
